name: storefront-tour
description: Twelve hand-authored natural-language questions over the bundled storefront package, written to vary grain, join depth, filter shape and answerability. Three ask for a business convention the model does not encode -- the company's summer window, net of cancellations and returns, and what counts as a customer -- one is deliberately open, and one has a silent wrong answer a careless grouping produces. Every case is `dev`: the set is a walkthrough meant to be run whole, so nothing is withheld from diagnosis. There is no holdout, so it cannot defend an acceptance check on a model edit without being re-split first.
conventions: Summer is the company's sales season, 25 May to 15 September inclusive. It is set by the buying calendar, not by the weather or the calendar quarter, and it does not move.
Net of cancellations and returns means excluding order lines whose status is Cancelled or Returned. Gross includes them.
A customer is someone who has placed an order that was DELIVERED -- not merely someone on the customer file, and not someone whose only orders were cancelled or returned.
sourceNote: Authored directly as a markdown numbered list in as-received/questions.md; one case per list item, question text copied byte for byte. No goldens arrived with them: every key here is derived by the conductor, first as DuckDB SQL over the raw parquet and then as Malloy through the truth package, and promoted only where the two agree.
auditNote: verify_goldens.py reports that dimension:customers:signup_date and products.retail_price do not appear in the model TEXT, and check_coverage marks the two cases that need them unanswerable. Both are wrong in the same way: those are columns the sources expose implicitly from the parquet, invisible to a grep of the .malloy and to a coverage judge reading only the model text. Both cases pass. Do not 'fix' those ids or declare the fields to silence the warnings. Nor fix the customers source's doc, which claims the table is people who have placed orders and is false for 26 of the 1,000 rows: a model that misdescribes its own table is part of what the customer question measures, and correcting the sentence hides the finding. The README's "Some of these SHOULD fail" section is the contract. check_findable.py returns 22 of 22 -- but only against a SEMANTIC, warm index. Without EMBEDDING_API_KEY the server matches on words and the same check reads about 14 of 22, and `ready` is necessary but not sufficient: a run immediately after it reported signup_date missing and the same id came back at relevance 1.0 seconds later. Re-run a single miss before believing it.
